title: Select the anti-rollback backend: HDP1-hidden unary flash-page counter owned by the pre-PIN stage (Trezor monoctr shape on the same silicon) instead of the stalled OTP codec
threat: Validly-signed downgrade to a vulnerable release. Today the floor can never move past its factory value: otp::bump_to has zero call sites, COMMIT refuses unconditionally, and the only selected physical backend (OTP quad-words) is invalid on STM32U585 ECC OTP, leaving every release the vendor ever signed installable forever (#31 ship-blocker).
proposal: Take an owner decision to route OPEN-OTP-1..3 to a non-OTP backend: one 8 KB bank-1 flash page per counter (security_epoch; optionally a second for release_version), encoded exactly as Trezor monoctr: value N == first N 16-byte quad-words programmed to 0x00, read rejects any programmed-after-erased gap, write refuses values below current and programs one fresh QW per increment with write->read->ensure, MONOCTR_MAX static-asserted against the largest epoch any release may carry. Place the page(s) at the start of the bank-1 secure area so HDP1 (SECWM1R2.HDP1EN + HDP1_PEND) covers FSBL pages 0..4 plus the counter page(s); the pre-PIN stage reads/bumps them, then sets FLASH_SECHDPCR.HDP1_ACCDIS before branching, so the mutable secure runtime can neither read nor forge the floor. Keep the counter page OUTSIDE the WRP range (WRP prevents the increment; Trezor's secret sector is pages 0-1 while WRP covers 2-13). Close #212 (OPTIGA E1E0 layer) as 'not needed' once this lands, and fold #39 (HDP1) into it.
rationale: This is the single most relevant vendor finding: Trezor solved the identical problem on the identical flash controller by moving the unary tally from OTP (F4) to an HDP-hidden ordinary page (U5), which U585 supports natively (one-shot QW programming, page erase only pre-lock, HDP temporal hiding until reset). It dissolves OPEN-OTP-1..3's 'one-program-only, interrupted program not retry-safe' blocker because a torn QW simply reads as programmed, and an 8 KB page gives 512 increments versus 64 QWs of OTP. It also gives invariant #10's FSBL an actual enforcement lever for the floor the runtime cannot lower even when fully compromised.

BitBox02 Nova ships bootloader anti-downgrade in hardware.
risks: Conflicts with the current strict reading that the FSBL has NO flash write path at all (marker.rs/invariant #10 consequence text) — needs an explicit owner exception limited to the counter page, or the bump must be done by the secure runtime BEFORE HDP engages (not possible: HDP is engaged by the FSBL before the runtime exists). HDP1 must be contiguous from page 0, so the counter page displaces Manifest A (page 5) in the frozen registry — a geometry change gated by #540/#758 and the Draft 1.1 digest. OPEN-ECC-1 does not vanish: a power-cut mid-program can leave an ECC-invalid QW that raises NMI on read; the reader must treat ECCD on a counter QW as 'programmed' deterministically and that needs sacrificial-silicon evidence. FSBL budget: a minimal program-QW path (~1-2 KB) against 38,912 B registry budget (28,704 B used) but only ~2 KB free on the bench 32 KiB linker. HDP also hides the FSBL's own vendor pubkey from the runtime — the runtime verifier must keep its own copy (it already does: secure/src/fw_update/vendor_pubkey.rs).
